name: Android: Split Screen with Two Apps
description: Run two apps side by side in split screen (multi-window) on the phone, so a person or an agent can work across both: Gemini next to a notes app, a chat app next to a browser, or copying from one app into the other. It is grounded on this phone through read-only adb checks (adb -s 127.0.0.1:5555 shell): Android 15 (SDK 35), a Motorola phone with the Motorola launcher (Recents is com.motorola.launcher3/com.android.quickstep.RecentsActivity), 1080x2400 at 400 dpi. `cmd activity supports-multiwindow` and `supports-split-screen-multi-window` both return true. The global settings enable_freeform_support, force_resizable_activities and enable_non_resizable_multi_window are already 1, and the template never changes them; any settings change is an optional step that needs the user's approval. The am command here has --windowingMode but no --activity-launch-adjacent option, so the adjacent flag is passed as raw flags (-f 0x10001000); `cmd activity task resize` and `stack list` exist. It documents four methods: (a) the Recents app-icon menu "Split screen" / "Rozdělit obrazovku" driven by UI automation, which is the stock route and the first one to try; (b) am start with --windowingMode (Android 12+ values: 1 fullscreen, 2 pinned, 5 freeform, 6 multi-window; the old 3/4 split values are gone) and FLAG_ACTIVITY_LAUNCH_ADJACENT plus NEW_TASK, marked unverified on this phone until the probe in the prompt has been run; (c) a Tasker or AutoInput route through the accessibility global action toggle split screen (AutoInput is installed, but its accessibility service was not enabled when this was written); (d) app pairs or launcher shortcuts. It also covers what uiautomator dumps look like with two windows (nodes from both packages, bounds in each half, the divider), how to target taps at one pane, keyboard and focus issues, verification with `cmd activity stack list`, how to leave split screen, the one-screen lock (one agent drives both panes), and the limits: some apps refuse resizing, the Gemini overlay is not a normal activity, landscape rotation changes the layout, and the PRoot reaches WindowManager only through adb. Use it when a task needs two apps visible at once, or when the user asks for a split-screen shortcut. Do not use it to copy text between apps when the clipboard is enough (`droid type`, the cliphist tools), for picture-in-picture video, or for desktop windowing on an external display. Pairs with: the android-control skill (`droid ui`, `droid tap`, `droid key recent`, `droid shot`, `droid sh`), the android-assistant MCP tools screen, act, open and run_tasker_task, the android-assistant skill, Tasker with AutoInput, tasker-edit.py tile for a Quick Settings tile, and /root/phone/state/agent.lock. Related prompts: android-automation-router (sends 'open Gemini and notes side by side' here), tasker-task-actions and tasker-profile-builder (the Tasker shortcut), tasker-direct-edit (the tile), android-app-agent-calibrate (when a driver breaks in a half-height window), android-proot-phone-ops, termux-proot-bridge. Variables: app_a - the first app, by name or package; it goes in the top or left pane ("Gemini, com.google.android.apps.bard"); app_b - the second app ("Keep, com.google.android.keep"); layout - top/bottom or left/right and the ratio ("top/bottom, 50:50"; portrait gives top/bottom, landscape gives left/right); purpose - what will be done across the panes, which decides where the keyboard goes ("read Gemini's answer, write notes in Keep"); persistence - one-off, Tasker shortcut, or QS tile ("one-off").
content:
# Split screen: {{app_a}} and {{app_b}}

Put the two apps side by side, verify the layout, then do the work across both panes.

## Inputs
- App A (top or left pane): {{app_a}}
- App B (bottom or right pane): {{app_b}}
- Layout: {{layout}}
- Purpose: {{purpose}}
- Persistence: {{persistence}}

## What this phone supports (read-only checks, November 2026)
Checked with `adb -s 127.0.0.1:5555 shell`, read-only. Run the same checks again before relying on them:
```
getprop ro.build.version.release; getprop ro.build.version.sdk       # 15, 35
cmd activity supports-multiwindow                                     # true
cmd activity supports-split-screen-multi-window                       # true
settings get global enable_freeform_support                           # 1
settings get global force_resizable_activities                        # 1
settings get global enable_non_resizable_multi_window                 # 1
dumpsys activity activities | grep -i windowing                       # mWindowingMode=fullscreen for every task
dumpsys activity recents | grep mRecentsComponent                     # com.motorola.launcher3/com.android.quickstep.RecentsActivity
cmd activity help | grep -i -A1 windowingMode                         # --windowingMode <WINDOWING_MODE>
settings get secure enabled_accessibility_services                    # AutoInput was not listed
```
- The display is 1080x2400 at 400 dpi, in portrait. All tasks were fullscreen and no split was active.
- The developer settings that force resizing are already on, so apps that declare themselves non-resizable can still be put in split screen. Do NOT change any of these settings. If the user wants one changed, describe the change, its effect and how to undo it, and wait for their approval.
- The `am` here has `--windowingMode` but no `--activity-launch-adjacent` option. The adjacent flag goes in as raw flags. Also present: `cmd activity task resize <TASK_ID> <L> <T> <R> <B>` (works only on multi-window or freeform tasks), `task resizeable`, and `stack list`.

## The lock
Split screen does not make two drivers possible. One agent drives both panes, under `flock /root/phone/state/agent.lock`, for the whole setup and the work that follows. Taps in one pane can move focus away from the other, and the Gemini overlay closes when another window takes focus.

## Methods (try in this order)
### (a) Recents app-icon menu, the stock route
1. Open B, then A (`open("<package>")` or `droid open <package>`), so that both have a Recents card and A is the newest.
2. `droid key recent` (KEYCODE_APP_SWITCH). Verify with `droid ui` that Recents is showing (package com.motorola.launcher3).
3. Tap A's app icon above its card (or long-press the card, depending on the launcher). A menu opens: "Split screen" / "Rozdělit obrazovku". Tap it.
4. A moves to the top half and Recents shows the other cards. Tap B's card.
5. Verify (see below). To swap the panes, double-tap the divider, if this launcher supports it.

### (b) am start with windowing mode or the launch-adjacent flag (unverified here)
Android 12 and later use these windowing modes: 0 undefined, 1 fullscreen, 2 pinned (PiP), 5 freeform, 6 multi-window. The old 3 and 4 (split primary and secondary) were removed in Android 12, so `--windowingMode 3` does not mean split screen on this Android 15. Split screen is now owned by SystemUI's window manager shell: two tasks in multi-window mode under a split root. Starting a task in mode 6 from the shell does not attach it to a split root. FLAG_ACTIVITY_LAUNCH_ADJACENT (0x1000) together with NEW_TASK (0x10000000) asks to launch next to the current task. It is honoured when the launching task is already in split, and from a fullscreen task it is often ignored. Probe before you claim anything, with the user's yes, under the lock. Each probe is reversible and changes no settings:
```
am start -n <B component> -f 0x10001000          # after A is in split via (a): does B replace the other pane?
am start --windowingMode 5 -n <A component>       # freeform window? (freeform support is on)
am start --windowingMode 1 -n <A component>       # back to fullscreen (the undo)
```
Record what each probe did in the report, and mark this method as verified or not.

### (c) Tasker or AutoInput
The accessibility global action "toggle split screen" (GLOBAL_ACTION_TOGGLE_SPLIT_SCREEN) splits the current app and opens the picker for the second one. AutoInput (com.joaomgcd.autoinput, installed) exposes it as a Global Action. Its accessibility service was not enabled when this was written, and enabling it is a settings change that needs the user's approval. Tasker may offer its own split-screen action, depending on the version, also through accessibility: check the action list. A shortcut task: launch B, launch A, toggle split screen, then pick B in the picker (by AutoInput or `droid tap`), and verify. Write it with `tasker-task-actions`, put a trigger on it with `tasker-profile-builder` if one is needed, and install it with tasker-import.sh.

### (d) App pairs and launcher shortcuts
Stock Android 15 can save an app pair from the Recents menu ("Save app pair"), which puts one home-screen icon that opens both apps in split. Whether this Motorola launcher offers it is unverified: look in the Recents menu while a split is active. If it is there, the pair icon is the cheapest way to make this persistent. Placing it on the home screen is a launcher change, so ask first.

## Verify the layout
```
cmd activity stack list | grep -E 'RootTask|taskId'
dumpsys window windows | grep -i -E 'divider|split'
```
Success: both tasks show visible=true, with bounds in different halves (top/bottom in portrait: roughly [0,0][1080,~1180] and [0,~1220][1080,2400]), and a divider window exists. A layout that gives a ratio other than 50:50 means dragging the divider. Use `act("swipe", ...)` from the divider's centre to the target y, then verify again. The default snap points are about 1:2, 1:1 and 2:1.

## Working across two panes
- **Dumps.** With two windows, `droid ui` / `screen()` should list nodes from both packages, each with bounds inside its own half, plus the divider. Check every node's package. If only the focused pane appears, tap a neutral area of the other pane to focus it and dump again, or use `droid shot`.
- **Targeting taps.** Filter the nodes by package and by the pane's bounds, and take coordinates from a fresh dump only. Stay at least 40 px away from the divider, because a drag there resizes the panes or closes one. Labels that exist in both apps (Search, Send, Share) are ambiguous: tap by #index or by coordinates inside the right pane.
- **Keyboard and focus.** Back and typing go to the focused pane. Tap the field in the target pane, confirm `focused` in the dump, then type. The keyboard covers the bottom half, so in top/bottom layout put the pane you type into ON TOP, as the purpose decides. The bottom pane shrinks or is hidden while the keyboard is up.
- **Copying between apps.** Use the clipboard: Copy in one pane, then long-press → Paste in the other, or KEYCODE_PASTE (279). Drag and drop between panes works for people but is unreliable for automation.
- **Leaving split.** Drag the divider to an edge, or run `am start --windowingMode 1 -n <component>`, or open Recents and tap the pair. Home leaves the pair intact in Recents.

## Limits
- Some apps refuse resizing (games, camera apps, some banking apps; never automate those anyway). The forced-resizable setting overrides most refusals, but layouts can break. Verify from a dump, not from the launch result.
- The Gemini overlay (googlequicksearchbox's robin MainActivity on top of the com.google.android.apps.bard task) is not a normal activity. It can close when the other pane takes focus. Put the full Gemini app task (com.google.android.apps.bard) in the pane and test whether ask_gemini's driver still finds the composer at half height. If it does not, calibrate it with android-app-agent-calibrate.
- Landscape rotation turns top/bottom into left/right and changes every pane's bounds. Dump again after any rotation.
- The PRoot cannot reach WindowManager directly. Everything goes through adb on 127.0.0.1:5555 (uid 2000) or UI automation. su commands need the user's yes.
- App drivers (chatbots.py, gemini.py) were calibrated fullscreen. In a pane, their scrolling and bounds heuristics may misfire.

## Persistence
- one-off: method (a) as one script under the lock.
- Tasker shortcut: the task from (c), or an app-pair icon from (d).
- QS tile: point a tile at that task with `tasker-edit.py tile N TASK "Split"` (the tasker-direct-edit procedure: pull, back up, push). Say which tile slot it replaces.

## Report
Methods tried and what each did (verified or not), the final bounds of both panes, the persistence set up and how to undo it, and any settings the user was asked about.
